column1: # LANES.tsv — one corpus per register, and which book each lane governs.
# WHAT THIS FILE IS
#   The register lane a ductus is measured against. A lane is a corpus, not a genre: the
#   books in it are all in the register a book in that lane should sound like. The ductus
#   names the lane in its Provenance, and `tools/prose/ductus-fit.py` measures the
#   resonant excerpts against that lane's documents. `tools/prose/corpus-report.py`
#   measures the lanes against each other and against the caps.
# WHAT A LANE IS NOT
#   - Not a bucket for books that share a subject. Three horror novels in three registers
#     are three lanes, or one bad lane.
#   - Not the slop rule set. The scanner's rules are shared and genre-free, and its
#     caps are GLOBAL: one set in deslop-check.sh serves every lane. So a cap re-derived
#     on a second lane moves the first lane's thresholds too. `corpus-report.py` prints
#     what each lane's own worst document would imply, because that is the evidence for
#     the decision; it does not make it. Per-lane caps need a scanner change and are a
#     freeze event (CORPUS_MAP.md section 6, ductus-designer open question 5).
#   - Not a place to park text. Corpus files stay local and untracked
#     (calibration/.gitignore); only this path is in the repository.
# SIZE
#   A lane is 5-10 works, roughly 500k-1M words, all in the target register. The caps are
#   set at 1.5x the worst single document, so a thousand-book lane would loosen every cap
#   toward meaninglessness and average the register into "books". The tools print the
#   measured size against this rule on every run; neither enforces it, because a lane
#   under construction has to be measurable to be finished.
# WHERE A LANE LIVES
#   `path` is where the lane belongs. A checkout may hold the corpus under a book's own
#   calibration directory instead - the copies .gitignore explicitly allows - and
#   `ductus-fit.py` resolves a missing registered path to exactly one such copy, printing
#   which one it used. Two copies is a refusal, not a guess.
# COLUMNS (tab-separated; a space-separated row is a parse error, not a guess)
#   lane     slug the ductus names
#   role     governing | control | planned | study  (only one governing lane per book)
#   register one line: what a book in this lane sounds like
#   books    works installed, as declared by the registry (corpus-report prints the
#            measured count beside it and calls a disagreement DRIFT)
#   words    measured words installed, as declared
#   path     repo-relative directory holding the documents
#   note     provenance and limits, one line
#   works    distinct works, when it differs from `books` (one series = one work)
#   era      when the prose was published. The axis that confounds every row that moved
#            after 1900; "unrecorded" is a true value and a guess is not.
#   status   INSTALLED | INSTALLED ELSEWHERE | NOT INSTALLED
#   answers  what this lane can actually settle
#   cannot   the questions it must never be asked
# The first seven columns are required and are read by header name; later columns may be
# added without touching a tool. Widened 2026-11-12 (CORPUS_MAP.md): the registry had a
# register and no era, no work count, and no statement of what a lane could answer.
